tables.how: Board files from 2014 to November 2026 whose short title contains 'Great Plates' or 'Feeding Services for Alternative Shelter': 7 files on 5 contracts. The amount before the first file of each contract is what it began at without a vote: Off the Grid Services LLC $9,405,000; San Francisco New Deal $9,108,000; San Francisco New Deal $9,917,050; SMG Food and Beverage LLC $9,479,817; Moonstar Buffet Restaurant $9,339,000. The case names four of the 5 contracts; the fifth, San Francisco New Deal's contract for shelter-hotel meals (File 210373), also began under the line, at $9,917,050. The four the case names began at $37,331,817 together and reached $120,150,483.
tables.limits: Amounts and names are read by rule from each file's title; the link opens the file itself, which governs. A title shows the latest version of the legislation, and a file that states no earlier amount cannot appear here. The contracts were signed in the first months of a declared emergency, when the number of people to be fed was not known and the State program was extended month by month; an amount set for a first term and raised as the program was extended is the ordinary reading. The titles do not say how each first amount was estimated.

sources.t: San Francisco Controller: Vendor Payments (Vouchers), fiscal 2019 to fiscal 2027 to date (DataSF)

tables.how: Every line of the Controller's payment file, fiscal 2019 to fiscal 2027 to date (to 9 November 2026), added up by payee, department, contract, purchasing rule and year. Two years are shown: the year the voucher was issued, read from its running number (scripts/lib/vouchers.py), and the fiscal year the file lists the line under, which for some lines is later. Kept: Human Services Agency payments to the payees that hold the contracts of the previous list. Through the years the case uses, they add up to $29,119,036 for Off the Grid (to fiscal 2023), $39,248,392 for SF New Deal (to fiscal 2022), $11,124,780 for Moonstar Buffet and $10,138,613 for SMG (to fiscal 2022). The case's $79,492,208 for the three Great Plates operators is the first three of those sums and counts every agency payment to them. Under the three contracts titled Great Plates alone the payments are $61,059,832 (Off the Grid $28,337,955, SF New Deal $21,597,097, Moonstar Buffet $11,124,780).
tables.limits: A payment is money paid for work under a contract, not a loss. The payment file starts in July 2018; near the turn of a year the voucher number dates a payment to within a few days. SF New Deal was also paid by the agency for shelter-hotel meals and for later grant programs, so its total is not all Great Plates money; the column 'Which agreement' separates them. The payment file does not give a count of meals.

tables.how: Projects of disaster 4482 (the coronavirus pandemic) with the City and County of San Francisco as applicant whose title contains 'GPD', the program's initials: 3 projects with approved costs of $61,293,197 and $59,600,503 obligated after $1,692,694 was taken back. Against all agency payments to the three operators the case counts $18,199,011 more paid than approved; against payments under the three contracts titled Great Plates the difference is $-233,365.
tables.limits: FEMA's records give approved costs by period, not by vendor, and do not say why money was taken back from the first project. The City's payments and FEMA's approved costs need not match: the federal share was 75 percent at first and the City could claim only eligible costs.
